small_guidance:
- The kernel currently launches one program per (N,C,Dp,Hp) = 32·64·8·16 = 262144 programs each doing only 32 elements of work — way too many tiny launches. Tile multiple Hp (and/or Dp) rows per program so each program does e.g. BLOCK_HP=4 or 8 output rows, amortizing weight/bias loads and reducing grid size by 4-8×.
- Add an autotune axis over BLOCK_HP ∈ {1,2,4,8} with num_warps ∈ {2,4} (BLOCK_W=64 is small, num_warps=2 likely best); also try keeping the LayerNorm gamma/beta in registers across the outer (dp,hp) tile loop instead of reloading.
- Avoid the `tl.reshape(acc, (BLOCK_W//2, 2))` + sum trick when W is not a power of 2 case; here W=64 so it works, but precompute even/odd masks to allow vectorized pooling without the reshape, which may permit larger BLOCK_W tiles fused across hp.
large_guidance:
- The dominant cost in this graph is `ConvTranspose3d` (output ≈ 32·64·16·32·32 fp32 with 3³ kernel and stride 2) — the post-conv fused kernel only touches the conv output, so even a perfect fused tail leaves the conv as the bottleneck. A from-scratch rewrite should replace the ConvTranspose3d itself with a custom Triton scatter-add kernel (input × weight outer product scattered into the strided/padded output grid) and fuse `+sum_weight`, LayerNorm-over-C-or-W, AvgPool3d, and GELU into the same producer's epilogue (or a chained pair of kernels) so the conv output is never materialized to global memory.
- Because LayerNorm is over the last dim (W=64) and AvgPool is 2×2×2, structure the conv kernel to produce a full W-row (or 2 adjacent W-rows for the depth/height pool partner) per program in registers, then do norm+pool+GELU before storing the pooled output directly — eliminating the 32·64·16·32·32 fp32 round-trip entirely.
- Use channels-last-3d (NDHWC) layout for the conv output staging so the LayerNorm reduction axis (W) is contiguous and pooling neighbors in D/H are easy to accumulate; fold conv bias into the epilogue add of sum_weight.
